desc: Ideation: identify the two-chain shortest common supersequence reduction and LIS-based LCS computation.

Implement the complete Python program: read N, X, A, B, P, Q from stdin with 0-indexing; build the red chain from P and A and the blue chain from Q and B by inverse-permutation traversal from X, returning impossible if any ball is outside X's cycle and otherwise returning vertices at distances M down to 1; compute the answer as len(red)+len(blue)-LCS, where LCS is the strict LIS of red positions mapped through the blue chain; print -1 if impossible, else the answer.

Verify the implementation on the provided samples and edge cases (no balls, balls already at X, fixed-point X, balls outside X's cycle, shared vertices in conflicting order), ensuring O(N log N) time, O(N) memory, and no hardcoded sample behavior.
